sections.h2: Choosing a way to sell in Hollywood
sections.html:
Three routes dominate in Hollywood: list with an agent, take a cash offer, or sell as is. How much work the house needs, how soon you must close, and whether a bank or a judge controls your calendar will steer the choice.

A listing gets the most eyes on the house but adds showings, loan approvals and an appraisal that can fall short. A cash offer drops most of those hurdles. Both paths finish at the Broward County records office with a witnessed deed, the transfer tax and recording.

  • Agent listing: biggest pool of shoppers, longer wait, outcome tied to a loan.
  • Cash or as-is buyer: few conditions, no repair demands, quick signing.
  • Sale to a relative: money still changes hands, so deed tax and homestead rules still apply.

Hollywood lies in southeastern Broward County, between Miami and Fort Lauderdale. The city covers about 30 square miles and is the third-largest municipality in Broward, home to 153,067 people in 2020 and an estimated 157,019 by mid-2025. Shoppers think of three zones: the barrier island on the Atlantic, the historic downtown around Harrison Street and Young Circle, and the western Hollywood Hills section.

Homeowners occupy 58.9 percent of housing, with a median value of $410,600 and a median rent of $1,653. About four in ten households rent, so landlords make up many of the sellers, and they face a different tax picture and closing checklist.

sections.h2: Beach, downtown or the west side
sections.html:
Where your house sits shapes who shops for it. The Broadwalk on the beach side runs nearly 2.5 miles past resort towers, condos and small inns, so buyers there are often thinking about condos, short stays or a second home. Downtown, around Harrison Street and Young Circle, mixes arts venues, bars and restaurants. The western Hollywood Hills area grew after Hollywood Boulevard was extended toward U.S. 27 in 1954.

The West Lake area borders the Anne Kolb Nature Center, which preserves more than 1,500 acres of mangroves. The Seminole Indian Reservation lies inside city limits as an independent entity. Describe the setting honestly in your listing or offer request and let the buyer judge the fit.

Public money can change what buyers will pay on a given street. Voters approved a $54 million bond in 2004 for public safety and parks, and a $165 million bond in 2019 for safety, technology, parks, neighborhood work and resilience. More than 30 projects were under construction under the later bond, and the city bought more than 45 acres of open space. Main roads are being rebuilt with bike lanes, wider sidewalks and bus bays.

If you are near the beach, downtown or a rebuilt corridor, mention these projects in the listing. Elsewhere, ask a local agent how your streets compare.

sections.h2: What happens to homestead when you sell
sections.html:
Living in the house means the exemption ends when you sell, and the buyer has to apply separately. Broward's property appraiser carries a seller's exemptions through the year of sale and no further.

A change of ownership also resets assessed value, so the buyer's first tax bill may be higher than yours, a point careful buyers raise while negotiating. If you will buy another Florida home, portability can carry part of your capped-value savings over once you file a homestead application, so ask the appraiser about it. The timely filing date is March 1, and the last possible late-filing day for tax year 2027 is September 20, 2027.

Landlords face a separate risk. Leasing a homestead house can forfeit the exemption, and a change nobody reported can trigger back taxes for up to ten years, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

sections.h2: Deed tax, recording fees and the tax calendar
sections.html:
Expect the state deed tax to be the biggest closing charge. It comes from section 201.02 at 70 cents per $100 of the price, and the state can pursue any party named on the document whatever the contract says. If a mortgage sits on the property, it counts as consideration whether or not the buyer takes it over.

The Broward clerk takes the tax at recording. Section 28.24 fees open at $5.00 for page one and climb with extra pages, extra names and technology charges. Your closing agent can total them for your deed.

The property tax bill works separately. Hollywood parcels are valued each January 1 and billed in November. A discount shrinks the longer you wait, and April 1 is when an open balance becomes delinquent. Your closing agent prorates the year between you and the buyer.

• Foreclosure: following a final judgment, the clerk schedules a public auction 20 to 35 days later unless the plaintiff allows more time. Closing your own sale first can head it off.
  • Probate: summary administration suits a smaller estate (up to $150,000 non-exempt) or a death more than two years back. Start with a lawyer who can list the creditor-claim deadlines.
  • Tenants: expect to give month-to-month occupants at least 30 days' notice, while a missed rent payment starts with a three-day written demand.

Deaths after 2004 carry no Florida estate tax.

sections.h2: What a landlord should do before selling
sections.html:
A tenant is the biggest unknown in a rented house. Gather each lease and every tenant's contact information, then decide whether the buyer will keep the tenancy or the house must be empty at closing. Because month-to-month occupants are owed at least 30 days' notice, begin that clock as soon as your plan is set.

Tell the Broward Property Appraiser about any change in use, since renting a homestead house can cost the exemption. A buyer who plans to keep tenants will want rent records, so have them ready alongside the tax bill.

sections.h2: Documents to gather for a cash offer
sections.html:
• The recorded deed and your latest tax bill.
  • A payoff letter for each mortgage or lien, plus estoppel details from a condo or HOA.
  • Copies of leases and tenant contacts.
  • A list of known repairs, open permits and storm claims.
  • For an estate, the court's letters of administration.

Florida requires two subscribing witnesses on a land conveyance. Book the signing around that, or use the remote witnessing the statute allows.

Once you accept an offer, the closing agent orders title work and requests a payoff from each lender. A condo or HOA supplies its own estoppel details. You sign the deed in front of two witnesses, and it is filed with the Broward clerk, who collects the transfer tax along with the recording fee.

A cash buyer takes loan underwriting out of the schedule, yet payoffs and recording still need days, so get a timeline in writing. Share leases, permit records and storm claim papers early. Late surprises are the usual cause of a delayed closing, and a tidy folder of documents prevents most of them.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair my Hollywood house first?
faqs.a: No. Cash and as-is buyers take the house in its present state and adjust their price. A buyer using a loan may still ask for fixes.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed tax in Hollywood?
faqs.a: The contract decides who pays in practice, though the state holds every party to the deed responsible. Confirm the line item with your closing agent.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The buyer files a new application, because your exemption ends with the year of sale.

faqs.q: What if back taxes are owed on my Hollywood home?
faqs.a: Usually the closing agent pays them from your proceeds after the Broward tax collector gives a payoff amount. Balances left unpaid are delinquent as of April 1.

faqs.q: How soon can a Hollywood sale close?
faqs.a: It depends on title work, liens and who is buying. Without a lender the process is shorter, yet payoffs and recording still take days, so request a written schedule.
